raw_case_text:
During the 2016 ZIKV outbreak in Merida, Mexico, a 27-year-old woman in the third trimester of pregnancy was referred to medical geneticist because multiple malformations detected in the fetus. Informed consent was obtained for sampling, clinical evaluations, and for the publication report. Exploring the medical records, she reported unquantified fever, preauricular nodes, pruritus and rash in the shoulder girdle and thorax in the first trimester when the pregnancy was unnoticed. No serological tests were performed for ZIKV at that time. Ultrasound was performed at 16.4 weeks of gestation with report of fetal growth within normal ranges; but at 23 weeks of gestation, the fetal hands were not identified. At 27.4 weeks of gestation, fetus was reported with microcephaly (DBP 58 mm); nuchal thickening, ventriculomegaly, hemisphere hypoplasia and cerebellar vermis were detected in the brain, and micrognathia, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis were also reported at that time.
A stillbirth with generalized subcutaneous edema was obtained via cesarean section at 35 weeks of gestation. At physical exploration showed craniofacial disproportion, microcephaly, irregular anterior and lower posterior hairline. Posterior sloping of the forehead and hypertelorism were observed. The nasal bridge, the nostrils and the filtrum were normal. Retrognathia and normal oral cavity were found. The ears were cupped with low implantation and thickened helix. The shoulders were short, with internal rotation and presented limitation to abduction. The left upper limb presented an extended elbow with limitation to the reduction, pronation arm, flexed wrist, non-reducible hand with cyanotic coloration. The upper right limb was conformed only to the proximal third of the arm. At this level, soft tissue defect was found with the presence of an irregular cutaneous line, exposure of subcutaneous tissue and the humeral condyle, no tissue bleeding was detected (Figure 1). The lower extremities presented limitation to hip abduction, knee extension and flexion of both feet. The genitalia anatomy showed 1 cm penis and a complete rough scrotum without testes inside.
On the skull x-ray, everted sutures and partial collapse of the cranial bones with a hypoplastic occipital was observed. The radiograph of the upper extremities shows a right humerus shorter than the left, with preserved of the distal region of the humerus (Figure 2). Computational axial tomography reported subcortical calcifications, lissencephaly, ventriculomegaly, and generalized cortical degeneration. The karyotype was normal, 46, XY. The serological test for toxoplasma, rubella, cytomegalovirus and herpes virus were negative in the mother and the patient. The RT-PCR for ZIKV/Dengue/Chikungunya in the patient's cerebrospinal fluid detected the presence of Zika viral RNA. Autopsy was not authorized.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 27-year-old pregnant woman in her third trimester was referred to medical genetics for evaluation of multiple fetal congenital malformations, including microcephaly, brain anomalies, arthrogryposis, and right upper limb radial/humeral deficiency, following a first-trimester febrile exanthem.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: During the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Merida, Mexico, the mother experienced unquantified fever, preauricular lymphadenopathy, pruritus, and a rash over her shoulder girdle and thorax during the first trimester (before she knew she was pregnant). Fetal ultrasound was normal at 16.4 weeks gestation, failed to visualize the fetal hands at 23 weeks, and at 27.4 weeks revealed severe microcephaly (biparietal diameter 58 mm), nuchal thickening, ventriculomegaly, cerebral hemisphere hypoplasia, cerebellar vermis anomalies, micrognathia, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis, prompting genetics referral and subsequent cesarean delivery of a stillborn male fetus at 35 weeks gestation.
subjective.past_medical_history: 27-year-old pregnant woman residing in Merida, Mexico, during the 2016 ZIKV epidemic; history of first-trimester febrile rash illness.
subjective.review_of_systems: Maternal history positive for first-trimester fever, preauricular lymphadenopathy, pruritus, and thoracic/shoulder rash.

objective.physical_examination: Physical examination of the 35-week stillborn male neonate: generalized subcutaneous edema, craniofacial disproportion, severe microcephaly, irregular anterior and low posterior hairline, posterior forehead sloping, hypertelorism, normal nasal bridge/nostrils/philtrum, retrognathia, normal oral cavity, and low-set cupped ears with thickened helices. Musculoskeletal and limb exam: short internally rotated shoulders with limited abduction; left upper limb with extended elbow, limited reduction, pronated forearm, flexed wrist, and non-reducible cyanotic hand; severe right upper limb transverse terminal reduction defect (amputation below the proximal third of the arm with an irregular cutaneous line, exposed subcutaneous tissue and humeral condyle, and no bleeding); bilateral lower extremities with limited hip abduction, limited knee extension, and bilateral foot flexion contractures (arthrogryposis). Genitalia: 1-cm micropenis and rugated scrotum with bilateral cryptorchidism (absent testes).
objective.routine_investigations: Prenatal ultrasonography (16.4, 23, and 27.4 weeks): progressive detection of absent fetal hands, microcephaly (BPD 58 mm), nuchal thickening, ventriculomegaly, cerebral hemisphere hypoplasia, cerebellar vermis anomaly, micrognathia, right radial aplasia, and arthrogryposis. Postnatal skull radiograph: everted cranial sutures, partial cranial bone collapse, and hypoplastic occipital bone. Upper extremity radiograph: shortened right humerus compared to the left with preservation of the distal humerus and absence of forearm/hand bones. Maternal and fetal TORCH serologies (Toxoplasma, rubella, CMV, and HSV): all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Postnatal cranial CT: subcortical calcifications, lissencephaly, ventriculomegaly, and generalized cortical degeneration. Fetal karyotype: normal male (46,XY). Fetal CSF multiplex RT-PCR for Zika, dengue, and chikungunya viruses: positive for Zika virus (ZIKV) RNA and negative for dengue and chikungunya.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Congenital Zika syndrome presenting with severe microcephaly, lissencephaly, subcortical calcifications, ventriculomegaly, arthrogryposis, cryptorchidism, and severe right upper limb transverse reduction defect (amniotic band-like/vascular disruption spectrum), resulting in stillbirth at 35 weeks gestation. Chromosomal abnormalities, TORCH infections (toxoplasmosis, rubella, CMV, HSV), dengue, and chikungunya were excluded. Confirmation: Detection of Zika virus RNA by RT-PCR in the stillborn infant's cerebrospinal fluid alongside normal 46,XY karyotype and characteristic neuroimaging and skeletal findings. Management and outcome: Delivered as a stillbirth via cesarean section at 35 weeks gestation; postmortem external, radiographic, cranial CT, cytogenetic, and CSF molecular evaluations were completed (full internal autopsy was declined by the family).
